content.heading: Welcome to RelayLab 360
content.body: RelayLab 360 is a protection relay test bench simulator. Use it to learn relay commissioning, configure protection settings, and simulate fault conditions in a safe virtual environment.

content.heading: Three Main Areas
content.body:
Field — physical wiring between the test suitcase and relay terminals.
Relay — phasor injection, protection settings, and relay behaviour.
Panel — circuit breaker panel and single-line diagram.

content.heading: Field Tab
content.body: The Field tab represents a physical test suitcase connected to a relay via a calibration switch and terminal block. Drag wires between compatible terminals to build the injection circuit.

content.heading: Terminal Naming
content.body:
i1_pos / i1_neg — current output jacks on the suitcase.
v1_pos / v1_neg — voltage output jacks.
bi1_pos / bi1_neg — binary input jacks.
bo1_pos / bo1_neg — binary output jacks.
tb_N_top / tb_N_bottom — terminal block openings (internally shorted).

content.heading: Calibration Switch
content.body: In the UP (closed) position the switch passes current through to the relay. In the DOWN position the S1/S2 banana jacks are shorted, providing a safe state when making connections.

content.heading: What is a Phasor?
content.body: A phasor represents a sinusoidal quantity by its magnitude and phase angle. The test suitcase injects these values into the relay's current and voltage inputs.

content.heading: Balanced 3-Phase
content.body: Use the '3φ Bal.' mode to automatically set Ib and Ic 120° apart from Ia. Choose ABC or ACB rotation sequence.

content.heading: Pre-Fault / Fault
content.body: Pre-Fault values are injected before the fault occurs. When Pre-Fault is enabled the simulation injects the pre-fault state for the configured duration, then switches to the fault state.

content.heading: ANSI/IEC Functions
content.body:
50/50N — Instantaneous overcurrent (phase / neutral).
51/51N — Time-overcurrent with IEC, US, IEEE, ANSI, or Definite-Time curves.
67/67N — Directional overcurrent using MTA angle and polarising voltage.
27/59 — Under/overvoltage with hysteresis.
47 — Negative-sequence voltage.

content.heading: Pickup and Time Dial
content.body: Pickup (Ipu) sets the threshold current in amps. Time Dial (TD) scales the operating curve. Higher TD = longer trip time.

content.heading: Output Matrix
content.body: The Output Matrix links each protection stage to relay binary outputs (BOs) and LEDs. A checked cell means that stage activates that output when it trips.

content.heading: Binary Outputs (BO)
content.body: BOs are physical output contacts on the relay that close when a protection stage trips. In the simulator they can be wired via the Field tab to open the circuit breaker.

content.heading: Binary Inputs (BI)
content.body: BIs receive external signals (e.g. circuit breaker status feedback). Use the Input Matrix to configure which BI corresponds to which function.

content.heading: LED Indicators
content.body: LEDs on the relay front panel illuminate when the assigned stage trips. They remain latched until manually reset.

content.heading: What is COMTRADE?
content.body: COMTRADE (IEEE C37.111) is a standard format for storing power system disturbance data. RelayLab 360 generates a three-file package: .cfg (configuration), .dat (sampled data), .hdr (header).

content.heading: How to Export
content.body: After a relay trip, open the Fault Records panel, select the trip record, and click Download. The files are packaged as a ZIP archive.

content.heading: Format Details
content.body: ASCII format, 960 samples/s, 8 analog channels: IA, IB, IC, IGS, VA, VB, VC, VN. The trip event is anchored at the 500 ms pre-trigger point.

steps.title: Welcome to RelayLab 360
steps.description: An integral platform for protection engineering. Click 'Next' to start the tour.

steps.title: Field Tab — Wiring Simulator
steps.description: Configure the physical test wiring. Connect the suitcase terminals to the terminal block and calibration switch.

steps.title: Relay Tab — Current Injection
steps.description: Inject three-phase currents and voltages to simulate faults. Configure phasors (magnitude and angle) to test different protection scenarios.

steps.title: Panel Tab — Circuit and Protection
steps.description: View the circuit breaker, command diagram (ladder) and single-line diagram. Monitor protection states and binary outputs.

steps.title: Protection Settings
steps.description: In the Relay tab, configure protection stages (50/51, 67, 27/59, etc.) with their technical parameters and characteristic curves.

steps.title: Run Simulation
steps.description: Click 'Inject' to start the simulation. The relay will detect the fault and trip the circuit breaker according to the protection settings.

customScenarios.title: Custom Scenarios
customScenarios.captureDesc: Phasors, matrices and all protection settings will be saved from current UI state.
customScenarios.info46: Pickup = I₂ (negative sequence) in secondary Amperes. Definite Time.
customScenarios.info81: 81U-1..3 = underfrequency · 81O-1..3 = overfrequency · Frequency set in the side panel (Frequency).
customScenarios.info32: 32R-1..2 = reverse power (P3φ < −pickup) · 32F-1..2 = forward power (P3φ > pickup) · Pickup in secondary Watts.
customScenarios.info79dead: Dead time = open time before reclosing. Reclaim time = time after successful reclosure to reset the shot counter.
customScenarios.infoCbOpened: Mapped BI receives signal when the breaker opens (52b contact). Trip time count stops at this instant.
customScenarios.infoCbClosed: Mapped BI receives signal when the breaker closes (52a contact). Logged in Event Log.
